newsitem.title: JAPAN: No broad Japan land remedy in March--govt sources.
newsitem.headline: No broad Japan land remedy in March--govt sources.

text.p: Japan's government is unlikely to unveil in March a package of steps aimed at boosting liquidity in the real estate market, government sources said on Thursday.

A source in the National Land Agency said there had been no consultations among various ministries about such a package of measures nor was any forum for drafting such broad measures likely to be set up soon.

Recently the stock market and other markets have been on an upswing on reports that the government would announce a broad package of steps to boost liquidity in the property market before the end of this fiscal year.

The agency source said that various ideas, including government purchases of land used as collateral for loans by failed housing-loan companies, or "jusen", were still being considered, but most land-related measures would not be carried out by the start of the new fiscal year in April.

The source also said that while land-related measures would be included in the government's late March update of its three-year comprehensive deregulation programme, they would only form a part of the broader programme.

Separately, a senior Ministry of Finance official said that government ministries are planning to issue an interim report containing proposals to boost liquidity in the land market and to promote securitisation of real estate collateral.
